name: application-course-progress-card
title: Course Progress Card
description: Course card with an SVG lesson-completion ring, title, a modules-remaining line, and a Continue learning CTA.
useWhen: Showing a user's progress through a specific course or curriculum on a dashboard or "continue learning" list.
You want a compact ring + count pairing rather than a full linear progress bar.
Distinct from Goal Progress Card, which shows target-vs-actual pacing (e.g. a savings goal) rather than a simple completed/total lesson count.
avoidWhen: You're showing a generic percentage with no course/lesson semantics — a bare Progress Ring or Progress Bar is simpler.
The course has no clear module count to complete against (e.g. open-ended reading) — a ring implies a countable finish line.
responsiveBehavior: The card is a fixed-width block; the ring and title/subtitle sit in a single row that doesn't reflow, with the Continue button spanning full width below.
accessibility: The percentage is rendered as text inside the ring, not conveyed by the arc length alone.
The modules-remaining line states the same progress as literal numbers ("7 of 10"), giving a redundant, unambiguous data point alongside the ring.
The ring's decorative SVG circles are aria-hidden; the surrounding text carries the accessible information.

variants.title: Course Progress Card
variants.description: An 'Advanced TypeScript Patterns' course at 70% (7 of 10 modules complete) with a Continue learning button.
accessibility: Percentage and module counts are both rendered as text, redundant with the visual ring.

variants.title: Course Progress Card (Dark)
variants.description: The same course progress card adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Ring track and fill colors remain distinguishable at dark-surface contrast.
